options.text: The AI can work in several languages.
options.explanation: That's multilingual. Multimodal is about types of input and output.

options.text: The AI can take in and produce different types of content, such as text, images, documents and audio.
options.explanation: Correct. Today's leading assistants are multimodal.

options.text: The AI runs on several devices.
options.explanation: That's cross-platform, not multimodal.

options.text: The AI uses several pricing plans.
options.explanation: Unrelated to multimodal.

questions.scenario: A damp-proofing company wants customers to upload a photo of the problem wall, and an AI to tell them whether it's rising damp, condensation or a leak, then quote automatically.

options.text: Go ahead: AI vision can diagnose damp reliably from photos.
options.explanation: Vision describes what's visible. It can't reliably diagnose causes that need on-site tests.

options.text: Use vision to describe the photo and collect details for the surveyor, to speed up triage, but keep diagnosis and pricing with a qualified person after a survey.
options.explanation: Correct. It uses the capability where it is mature (reading and describing) and keeps diagnosis with a qualified person.

options.text: Don't use photos at all.
options.explanation: Too cautious. Photos plus an AI summary can make the surveyor's triage much faster.

options.text: Use image generation to show customers what their wall will look like.
options.explanation: This doesn't address the request and risks misleading customers.

questions.prompt: Which capability is generally the MOST mature and reliable for small-business use today?

options.text: Fully autonomous agents that run the business's admin unsupervised
options.explanation: Agents are useful with supervision, but not mature enough to run unsupervised on important work.

options.text: AI video generation for adverts
options.explanation: Still experimental for most small businesses: short, inconsistent clips.

options.text: Speech-to-text transcription of voice notes and meetings
options.explanation: Correct. Transcription is reliable and widely built into tools already.

options.text: Measuring room dimensions from a single photo
options.explanation: Precise measurement from photos is a known weak spot.

questions.prompt: A kitchen fitter wants to post AI-generated images of 'our latest kitchen installations' on their website. What's the issue?

options.text: None. Images are just marketing.
options.explanation: Presenting generated images as real work misleads customers.

options.text: It misleads customers and can breach UK advertising rules (the CAP Code). Use real photos, or clearly label concept images.
options.explanation: Correct. Generated images are fine for concepts and graphics, but never passed off as real completed work.

options.text: Image generators can't create kitchens.
options.explanation: They can, and very convincingly, which is exactly the problem.

options.text: It's only a problem if the images are low quality.
options.explanation: Quality doesn't matter. Misrepresentation is the issue.

questions.prompt: Which of these are examples of chaining capabilities together? Choose all that apply.

options.text: Voice note → transcription → AI turns it into a structured job sheet
options.explanation: Yes: voice, then text, then structure.

options.text: Photo of a delivery note → data extraction → new row in a job-costing spreadsheet
options.explanation: Yes: vision and documents, then structured data.

options.text: Typing a question into ChatGPT and reading the answer
options.explanation: That's a single capability (text in, text out), not a chain.

options.text: Missed call → automatic text asking what they need → AI classifies the reply and drafts a callback note
options.explanation: Yes: automation plus text classification plus drafting.
